claim_boundary: The W=0 support classification is exact and includes the two-column sign-flip exception.
The same-column completion forces nonzero aggregate K5 unless every term is row-separated.
The row-separated branch is not excluded: no 49-term decomposition is constructed, and no tensor-rank lower bound 50 is proved.
Simple-matroid openness and ordinary flattenings do not close either remaining branch.
A-CLOSED, ordinary lower 50, and border rank remain unresolved.

exact_remaining_component.definition: Z_A_grad_hess_W0 intersect {all same-column Hessian witnesses vanish}
exact_remaining_component.equality_problem_on_this_component: any true identity here is a 49-term simple-tensor decomposition of the 7 by 7 permanent tensor
exact_remaining_component.name: Z_A_row_separated_49
exact_remaining_component.off_row_hessian_role: the nonzero off-row targets become the mixed flattening equations of that simple-tensor decomposition
exact_remaining_component.pigeonhole_reason: each row supports at most one factor, while seven nonzero factors must occupy the seven available rows
exact_remaining_component.structure_theorem: each of the 49 terms has, after permuting its seven factors, exactly one nonzero linear factor in each matrix row

flattening_boundary.consequence: ordinary row-bipartition flattenings give only the lower bound 35 and therefore do not exclude 49 terms

same_column_completion.consequence_on_W0: if two factor slices are nonzero at one row, then some same-column witness is nonzero, hence the aggregate global K5 is nonzero

smallest_remaining_invariant: either force a nontrivially paired K2 vector on the nonzero-Hessian-witness branch, or prove tensor rank(permanent_7) at least 50 on Z_A_row_separated_49 using a stronger-than-flattening invariant

wzero_row_slice_classification.statement: at a fixed term and row, a W=0 family is exactly one of: at most one nonzero slice; arbitrarily many slices on one common column; or two slices on the same two columns with sign-flipped proportional coefficients
wzero_row_slice_classification.support_at_least_three_consequence: every other factor slice at that row is zero
wzero_row_slice_classification.support_one_consequence: all nonzero slices use that same single column
wzero_row_slice_classification.support_two_consequence: at most one other slice is nonzero; it has the same two-column support and is sign-flipped proportional
